summary: A pull request summary is the JSON file the summarize-pr skill writes to explain a pull request. It sorts the changed files into groups in reading order and attaches review notes to groups, files, and lines. The project CLI checks that file against the pull request's diff and stores both on a hidden Git ref, refs/projector/summaries. The repository's Projector site renders each stored summary as a page like this one. Until this change, the code, the CLI flags, and the docs called that file a spec.

Projector's planning skill is about to be renamed spec, which would give the word two meanings. This change gives the file the name it already had on disk. The CLI's --spec flags become --summary, publish stores summary.json instead of spec.json, and the site build reads only summary.json. Every Python name, skill passage, and document that meant a summary now says summary. The JSON keys inside the file and its version do not change.

The change keeps no compatibility with the old names, because Projector is at version 0. A summary stored as spec.json stays off the site until someone republishes it with a release that writes summary.json, and the released CLI, 0.6.9, still writes spec.json. Instead of dropping such a summary silently, the site build now reports each one as a skipped review, and docs/site.md gives the commands that republish it. One review finding is open, flagged below: a republished summary takes the republish as its date, so the order you republish a pull request's heads in decides which one the site calls newest.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Summary: the JSON file a page is built from, holding the pull request's base and head, an overview, and groups of files with notes.
  • Summaries ref: refs/projector/summaries, a hidden Git ref that is not a branch. It holds one summaries/<number>/<head>/ folder per published head, with the summary and its diff.patch. The site's GitHub Action builds the site from it.
  • Walkthroughs: the name summaries had before an earlier rename. A repository that has not published since then keeps its summaries on refs/projector/walkthroughs, under walkthroughs/.
  • Released CLI: the project command from the latest release, 0.6.9, which still writes spec.json.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• This pull request replaces #175, which was closed with the same branch at the same head. The review of 661aad4 raised two findings, first raised on #175: the site build dropped every summary stored as spec.json without a report, and the docs said a walkthroughs-era site keeps working.
  • Both are fixed at this head. Against a copy of the real summaries ref, which holds 19 spec.json summaries, the build writes 0 reviews, 19 reviews skipped, and against the walkthroughs ref it writes 0 reviews, 2 reviews skipped.
  • The review of this head opened one finding, on the republish procedure the fix adds, flagged on summary_time below.
  • The validation gate (440 tests), the TypeScript checks, and the build pass. The merge from main keeps both sides of its one conflict.

cards.title: What it leaves for later
cards.html:
• The migration from the walkthroughs ref still copies that ref's spec.json files onto the summaries ref, where the build reports them as skipped. The pull request body leaves its removal to a later change.
  • Three uses of the word stay because they mean something else: test-file patterns such as .spec.ts, an importlib module spec in tests/test_release.py, and the historical path in the completed pr-walkthrough plan. Every other spec.json names the file older releases stored.

groups.title: The CLI's flags and the stored file
groups.kicker: What a user types, and what lands on the summaries ref
intro: Three project commands take a summary file. summary init writes a skeleton, summary publish checks the file against the diff and commits both to the summaries ref, and site page builds one page from the file. Each now takes --summary where it took --spec. An old command line fails with argparse's the following arguments are required: --summary and exit status 2, so nothing runs with the wrong file.

summary.py owns the file format and publishing. Its change is a rename throughout: the error type, the version constant, the helpers, the docstrings, and the messages. The one change in behavior is the file name that summary_tree writes on the ref.

checks.text: The JSON inside the file is unchanged. It has the same keys, and version is still 1. Only the file's name on the ref and the names in the code change.

files.note: The summary format, its checks, and publishing to the summaries ref. Everything here is renamed, summary_tree writes the new file name, and LEGACY_SUMMARY_FILE names the old one.

checks.text: LEGACY_SUMMARY_FILE is the name older releases stored each summary under. The site build uses it only to find and report summaries it will not read.
summary_tree now writes summary.json beside diff.patch. Republishing an old head adds this file beside its spec.json, which stops the build reporting that head.

The walkthroughs migration still runs here. It replays the old ref's commits onto the summaries ref, keeping their dates, but those commits hold spec.json files, which the site reports as skipped rather than reads.

With a seed that holds only spec.json files, the new tree always adds this head's summary.json, so the seeded branch below, which reuses the seed as the commit, no longer runs for a real ref. The review suggests removing it.

SUMMARY_VERSION stays 1, although a renderer from this change no longer reads version-1 summaries stored as spec.json. The completed pr-walkthrough plan makes this version the compatibility contract for the @v0 action: every renderer on a major tag accepts every summary of the version it shipped with. The review suggests shipping this change in a minor release whose notes tell repositories to republish their summaries.

files.note: Renames the three --spec flags to --summary, their help text, and every caught SpecError.

checks.text: The file site page reads is called data, not summary. A local named summary anywhere in run_site would shadow the summary module this file imports, and the status branch of the same function, which calls summary.hosting, would raise UnboundLocalError. Checked by reading run_site and its imports; the unit suite passes at this head.

groups.title: The site build and its action
groups.kicker: Where the site finds summaries, and which files it builds
intro: The site is built by project site build, which the repository's GitHub Action runs after every publish, and by project site serve for a local preview. Both extract the summaries ref into a directory and hand it to build_summaries. That function builds a page for every summary it finds and reports any it cannot build as an ::error annotation in the deploy log.

build_summaries builds only <number>/<head>/summary.json. It reports each spec.json that has no summary.json beside it as a skipped review, with an annotation telling the reader to run project upgrade and republish it, and the deploy still succeeds. Each pull request's heads are ordered by summary_time, the commit that last touched each summary.json; the open finding is about that date.

files.note: build_summaries globs the new file name and reports the old one. The rest is renamed variables and docstrings.

checks.text: Open review finding: republishing a pull request's old heads can make an older head its newest page. summary_time dates each summary by the last commit that touched its summary.json, so a summary republished as docs/site.md describes is dated at the republish, not when its head was published. Republish two heads of one pull request newest first, and the older head becomes the page reviews/<number>/ serves and the head the list marks current. A ref built that way at this head serves the older head. seed_from_legacy's docstring still says the replay keeps each summary's publish date for this ordering, but those dates are on spec.json files the site does not read. The finding's fix: date a summary.json that has a spec.json beside it by the spec.json's commit, or else tell readers to republish each pull request's heads oldest first.

Every spec.json without a summary.json beside it is reported, and a republished head is not. Built against a copy of the real summaries ref, which holds 19 spec.json summaries, this head writes 0 reviews, 19 reviews skipped with one ::error annotation per summary; test_a_summary_stored_as_spec_json_is_reported_until_it_is_republished covers the republished case.

The local summary in build_summaries shadows nothing. This module imports DIFF_FILE, LEGACY_SUMMARY_FILE, SummaryError, and prepare_page from ..summary by name, not the module itself. Checked by reading the module's imports.

files.note: Docstrings only. site serve extracts the summaries ref, or the walkthroughs ref when no summaries ref exists, and the build above decides which files count.
Renames the fetch step to Fetch the summaries, and the worktree it checks the ref out into to summaries-ref.

checks.text: tests/test_site.py finds this step by its exact name, to run its script against temporary remotes, so the step name and that test change together.

The fallback still points the build at walkthroughs/ when a repository has no summaries ref. A real walkthroughs ref holds spec.json files, which the build reports as skipped: this repository's two give 0 reviews, 2 reviews skipped.

intro: The browser renders each summary page from its data.json with site/src/summary.ts. The repository commits the compiled site/assets/summary.js, because every deploy and every CLI install reads it from a Git tree. The change renames renderFile's parameter, which holds one file's entry in a group, from spec to entry, and rewords two comments.

checks.text: This file matches its source. At this head, npm ci, npm run check, and npm run build in site/ pass and leave it unchanged.

groups.title: The skills
groups.kicker: What agents are told to write and run
intro: summarize-pr is the skill that writes summaries. Its format reference, renamed from spec.md to format.md, documents the JSON. Both now say summary, and every command in them uses --summary. review-pr tells the review loop to start a new head's summary from the earlier head's, and writing.md uses the word in two examples.

checks.text: An agent reads these files from its installed plugin and runs the project CLI it has installed, and the two update separately. Until both come from a release that includes this change, a mismatched pair fails with a usage error that names the flag the CLI expects.

files.note: Every --spec becomes --summary, and the stored file is summary.json.

checks.text: The skill now tells an agent that a summary stored as spec.json is off the site, and to update one by starting from its spec.json and publishing it as summary.json.

intro: docs/cli.md and docs/site.md describe the current behavior, so they follow the rename. The four plans are all completed, so none makes a readiness claim. The change rewrites the word in their design text too, and keeps one historical path in pr-walkthrough that names what the retired walkthroughs ref holds.

checks.text: The new section's commands copy a stored spec.json to summary.json and publish it. For each of this repository's 19 stored summaries, GitHub's compare API still serves the diff from its pr.base to its pr.head, and the summary builds against it. It says nothing about order, which the flag on summary_time is about.
This paragraph now says the workflow keeps deploying but the old summaries are reported as skipped, and points at the republish section.

The walkthroughs paragraph now says the old summaries are all spec.json and drops its claim that the replay keeps the dates the site orders heads by.
This path keeps spec.json on purpose. It names the files that the retired walkthroughs ref holds.
